items.text: Northwind Payroll Update: Effective March 1, all salaried employees move to semi-monthly pay periods. Direct deposit details will refresh automatically, and confidential earnings statements remain accessible only through the HR portal.
Episode 42 of The Quiet Signal is out now — we dig into how small teams set administrator permissions without stepping on each other. Listen wherever you get your podcasts.

We finally picked a date for the wedding — June 14th at the Rosewood Barn, with the ceremony starting at 4 p.m. Noella is handling the florist and I'm on catering, so please send any dietary notes her way by May 1. The venue has a strict noise rule after 10 p.m., which means the band wraps up a little earlier than we'd hoped. Parking is limited, so we're encouraging carpools from the Miller Street lot. Save-the-dates go out next week.

Here's the summary of our payroll vendor migration. The finance system will lock timesheet edits at noon on Friday so the export can run cleanly. Administrators in each department should double-check cost-center codes before then. Confidential bonus figures are handled separately and won't appear in this export. If something looks wrong after Monday, email payroll-ops@brightfieldcpa.example and we'll trace it.
Reminder: the podcast's bonus episode on remote onboarding drops Thursday, and the transcript will be posted on the same page.

Wedding planning checklist for the Hartley–Okafor wedding: confirm the caterer's final headcount by June 1, send the revised seating chart to the venue coordinator, and collect the rings from the jeweler the week before. Uncle Ray has offered to run the sound system, though he'll need access as a guest administrator on the venue's booking portal. The photographer wants a shot list by mid-May. Keep the budget spreadsheet confidential — it's shared only with the two families.
The payroll portal will be down for scheduled maintenance Saturday from 6 to 9 a.m.; plan any timesheet corrections around that window.

In this week's episode, host Priya Raman talks with a labor lawyer about the new overtime rules taking effect in July. They walk through which roles are affected and how to read the updated pay stub. There's also a short segment on why your employer's system might show a slightly different net figure the first pay period after a raise. Full show notes and a transcript are below.

A note from the payroll team at Larkin & Doyle: your direct deposit split changed on the January statement, so the amounts going to your savings account will look different this month. The system applies splits in the order listed on your profile, and any change takes one full cycle to appear. Confidential salary review documents stay with HR and are never attached to pay stubs. Questions go to the payroll desk on the third floor.
Postponed: the wedding rehearsal dinner moves to Friday the 13th at 7 p.m. at the Harbor Grill; the restaurant's administrator confirmed the room today.
